subject: Pricing & caching assumptions — follow-up from today's call
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom@fastretail.com>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing & caching assumptions — follow-up from today's call

Thanks again for taking time today, Tom + Sara — really useful conversation. Quick recap and next steps on the pricing/caching items we discussed.

Recap of your ask:
- Monthly logical volume: you mentioned ~30-50M tokens to start, ramping to 100M+ in 6-12 months.
- Budget target: you called out a target of roughly $800–$1,000 per 1M logical tokens as a target budget to make this feasible.
- Workload: mix of assistant chat (multi-turn), product search reranking, and some high-reuse responses for templated flows (order status, returns).

Our assumptions and quick math (see attached "redwood-pricing-estimates.pdf"):
- Base raw compute list price (example model profile): $1,400 per 1M model tokens (generation + context costs). This is the baseline we use to illustrate unit economics before caching/discounts.
- Caching approach: prefix (prompt) caching + response-level caching for high-reuse templates. We generally apply cache hit rate to the fraction of tokens that are cacheable (prefix and/or repeated response text). For simplicity below we model effective billed tokens ~= (1 - hit_rate) * logical_tokens.

Example effective $/1M logical tokens by hit rate (simple model):
- 20% hit rate -> effective cost = $1,400 * (1 - 0.20) = $1,120 per 1M
- 40% hit rate -> effective cost = $1,400 * (1 - 0.40) = $840 per 1M
- 60% hit rate -> effective cost = $1,400 * (1 - 0.60) = $560 per 1M

Notes on hit-rate drivers:
- Template-heavy flows (order confirmations, fixed replies) often achieve 50–70% response-level reuse.
- Chat assistants with long, unique user prompts typically get lower response-level reuse but can still benefit from prefix/KV caching across sessions (we see 20–40% in many chat pilots).
- Effective savings depend on which portion of the token budget is cacheable (e.g., if only prefixes are cacheable and they represent 40% of tokens, a 50% prefix hit rate yields a 20% overall hit).

Action items / next steps:
1) Can you confirm a narrower monthly token range for FY1 (we used 30–50M in the attached calc)?
2) If possible, share a small anonymized sample (5–10k requests) or an excerpted prompt corpus we can use to estimate an expected cache hit rate and model selection (I can provide an upload link).
3) I attached a one-page pricing estimate and a draft SOW for procurement. We can iterate on discounts for committed volumes.

If it helps, happy to run a quick sensitivity table on effective $/1M under a few different cache-hit and cacheable-fraction assumptions once we have sample data. Proposed follow-up: 30-minute call next week to go over the SOW and the hit-rate results.

Thanks —
Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-pricing-estimates.pdf (1 page)
Attachment: sow-draft.docx (stub)

From: Tom Nguyen <tom@fastretail.com>

Cc: Sara Lee <sara.lee@fastretail.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing & caching assumptions — follow-up from today's call

Hey Marissa — thanks for the summary and the clear examples. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Volume: realistic FY1 plan is closer to 30–40M logical tokens/month (we're being conservative on ramp).
- Budget: our internal threshold is about $900 per 1M logical tokens — anything materially above that becomes hard to justify without clear ROI.
- Expected hit rates: for our most common templated flows (order status / shipping updates) we expect ~55% reuse. For chat (customer support assistant) probably closer to 20–30% overall. So blended we'd estimate ~35–45% if prefix caching is effective.
- Peak: day peak QPS may spike during promotions; we care about a predictable burst policy and predictable unit economics.

Yes — we'll try to pull a small request sample for you (anonymized). Sara on procurement is cc'd and will coordinate the SOW review.

Can you also include an example showing the effect of a prefix-only cache vs. full response cache? That helps our engineering team understand the value of investing in client-side prompt standardization.

—Tom
Head of Product, Fast Retail Co.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom@fastretail.com>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing & caching assumptions — follow-up from today's call

Great — thanks Tom, that's super helpful. Quick follow-up with the two cache-mode examples you asked for and a couple of ballpark numbers using your FY1 volume range (30–40M/month):

Assumptions (for the examples below):
- Baseline raw list price: $1,400 per 1M billed tokens (model profile w/ standard context).
- "Logical tokens" = the tokens your app emits/consumes as measured in observability/usage.
- Effective billed tokens = logical_tokens * (1 - overall_hit_rate). We split examples by cache scope below.

1) Prefix-only cache (prefix represents ~45% of tokens in your flows; prefix hit rate = 50%):
- Overall hit rate = prefix_fraction * prefix_hit_rate = 0.45 * 0.50 = 0.225 (22.5%)
- Effective cost per 1M logical tokens = $1,400 * (1 - 0.225) = $1,085 per 1M
\2) Full-response cache (applies to templated responses; blended response hit = 50%, overall cacheable fraction = 35%):
- Overall hit rate = 0.35 * 0.50 = 0.175 (17.5%)
- Effective cost per 1M logical tokens = $1,400 * (1 - 0.175) = $1,155 per 1M
\Note: the examples above show that prefix caching can be more valuable than response-only caching for your specific token mix because prefixes make up a larger share of tokens. If you can standardize prompts (client-side templating) that increases prefix hit rate and moves effective cost down quickly.
\Sensitivity quick table (baseline $1,400 raw):
- 20% overall hit -> $1,120 / 1M
- 30% overall hit -> $980 / 1M
- 40% overall hit -> $840 / 1M
- 50% overall hit -> $700 / 1M
\Ballpark for Fast Retail (30–40M/month):
- If blended overall hit = 35% -> effective ~$910 / 1M (aligns with your $900 target)
- If blended overall hit = 45% -> effective ~$770 / 1M
\Next steps I propose:
- You share a small anonymized sample (5–10k requests) and I will run a quick hit-rate analysis + refined pricing table.
- We lock in a follow-up 30-min call next Wed (Mar 30) to review results and the SOW.
- Marcus (cc) will prepare a committed-volume discount schedule keyed to 6- and 12-month commits so procurement has something concrete for Sara.
\Sara — I'll send a versioned SOW and a redlined example for your procurement review.
\Thanks — talk soon.
Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
